commands.name: csv_sort
commands.description: Opens a CSV in Calc, sorts its rows by one column (the header row stays first), saves the result as a new CSV, checks it by reading it back, and closes it.

args.name: path
args.meaning: The CSV file to sort; not changed.

args.name: column
args.meaning: The exact header of the column to sort by.

args.name: to
args.meaning: The new CSV file; must not exist and must end in .csv.

args.name: descending
args.meaning: Sort Z to A / largest first.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": LibreOffice has no scripting for this.

example_requests: Sort employee_list.csv by last name and save it as a new file
Order this CSV by the Points column, highest first
Sort the spreadsheet by city in LibreOffice
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: A new CSV at to holds the same header and rows, sorted by the column; the source is unchanged and no LibreOffice window for it is left open.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: a suffix is wrong, two columns share the name, or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: NotFound
errors.when: no such file, or no such column in the first row

errors.name: AlreadyExists
errors.when: to already exists; nothing is overwritten

errors.name: OutsideAllowedRoot
errors.when: CALC_ALLOWED_ROOT is set and a path is outside it

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: a document with the source's or target's name is already open, LibreOffice shows Document Recovery, or another app came to the front

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the saved file wasn't sorted with the same rows

errors.name: NotSupported
errors.when: mode is "background"

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with LibreOffice 26.8.1.1 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.

LibreOffice ignores the Accessibility press on the Sort dialog's labels checkbox and order buttons, so each is clicked at the left end of its own frame if its value didn't change, then read again; never fixed screen positions.
Cells LibreOffice changes on import (leading zeros, trailing decimal zeros, dates) would change in the saved file; the read-back check reports that as UIError.

commands.name: csv_convert
commands.description: Saves a CSV file as a new Excel .xlsx or OpenDocument .ods spreadsheet with File > Save As…, checking every cell by reading the file back.

args.name: to
args.meaning: The new file, ending in .xlsx or .ods; it must not exist.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": LibreOffice has no scripting for this.

example_requests: Convert this CSV to an Excel file
Turn the CSV into an OpenDocument spreadsheet
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: A new spreadsheet at to holds the CSV's cells; the CSV is unchanged and no LibreOffice window for it is left open.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: path isn't a .csv, to doesn't end in .xlsx or .ods, the CSV is empty, or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: NotFound
errors.when: no file at path

errors.name: AlreadyExists
errors.when: to already exists; nothing is overwritten

errors.name: OutsideAllowedRoot
errors.when: CALC_ALLOWED_ROOT is set and a path is outside it

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: a document with the source's or target's name is already open, LibreOffice shows Document Recovery, or another app came to the front

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the saved file's cells don't match the CSV

errors.name: NotSupported
errors.when: mode is "background"

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with LibreOffice 26.8.1.1 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
Cells LibreOffice changes on import (leading zeros, trailing decimal zeros, dates) would change in the saved file; the read-back check reports that as UIError.
Added overnight in its own section and tested on its own.

commands.name: spreadsheet_to_csv
commands.description: Saves the first sheet of an .xlsx or .ods spreadsheet as a new CSV file with File > Save As…, checking it by reading it back.

args.name: to
args.meaning: The new CSV file; it must not exist.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": LibreOffice has no scripting for this.

example_requests: Export this Excel file as CSV
commands.precondition: The program has Accessibility, and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: A new CSV at to holds the first sheet's cells; the spreadsheet is unchanged and no LibreOffice window for it is left open.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: path isn't an .xlsx or .ods that can be read, to doesn't end in .csv, or mode isn't "ui" or "background"

errors.name: NotFound
errors.when: no file at path

errors.name: AlreadyExists
errors.when: to already exists; nothing is overwritten

errors.name: OutsideAllowedRoot
errors.when: CALC_ALLOWED_ROOT is set and a path is outside it

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: a document with the source's or target's name is already open, LibreOffice shows Document Recovery, or another app came to the front

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared, or the CSV's cells don't match the first sheet

errors.name: NotSupported
errors.when: mode is "background"

known_gaps: Verified on macOS 15.6.1 with LibreOffice 26.8.1.1 only, so it isn't known to work on macOS 26 or any other version.
It depends on English names and was tested only in English.
Only the first sheet is saved; only spreadsheets of plain text and whole numbers were tested.
Added overnight in its own section and tested on its own.
